item1.justification: The trace misapplies §102 by treating claim 6 as an “obvious variation” and provides no Graham/KSR analysis for §103, instead defaulting to non-obviousness when the LLM was unavailable.

item2.justification: Although the §102 rejection identifies claim features and US-2013196654-A1, every §103 conclusion lacks claim comparisons, prior-art analysis, and supporting evidence.

item3.justification: The office action and final decision consistently adopt the novelty-stage claim dispositions, while expressly deferring §103 because that analysis was unavailable.

item4.justification: The examiner’s high claim-breadth setting is reflected in expansive inherent-disclosure and equivalence readings, while the moderate strictness and combination threshold are not materially contradicted.

item5.justification: The final rejection follows the office action’s §102 rejection of the same ten claims and separately recommends amendment of the claims previously identified as novel.
